guesses.reason: Short dense coat with gray mackerel tabby striping overlaid by soft peachy-orange patches on the back and a warm cream hind paw is the classic torbie pattern of a random-bred shorthair.
The muted blue-gray base and pale apricot patches could also read as a dilute tortie-tabby coloring.
The tabby striping and moderate, balanced build loosely echo the American Shorthair, though the lean frame and larger ears point to a typical domestic mix.

breed.appearance: A slender young adult shorthaired cat with a cool gray mackerel tabby coat marked by thin dark stripes along the sides and legs, with soft peach-orange patches blended across the back and shoulders and a pale apricot-cream rear paw. The face has a classic tabby 'M' on the forehead, dark lines running from the eyes, a whitish muzzle and chin with long white whiskers, a dusty pink nose, and wide, round golden-green eyes. Large upright triangular ears with pinkish insides and light ear tufts sit atop a wedge-shaped head, and the cat wears a thin dark collar.
breed.fun_fact: Torbie cats combine tabby stripes with tortoiseshell patches, so every one wears a one-of-a-kind coat, and Kimball comes with a built-in best friend, Damen!
